page: Context Storage Middleware for storing Hono Context in AsyncLocalStorage for global accessibility. Import: {Hono} from 'hono', {contextStorage, getContext, tryGetContext} from 'hono/context-storage'. Runtime requirement: AsyncLocalStorage support. Cloudflare Workers: requires nodejs_compat or nodejs_als flag in wrangler.toml. Type-safe with Env generic <Env>. Access patterns: getContext<Env>().var for variables, getContext<Env>().env for bindings. Functions: contextStorage() middleware, getContext<Env>() returns Context or throws, tryGetContext<Env>() returns Context or undefined. Type definitions: Env { Variables: {message: string} }, Env { Bindings: {KV: KVNamespace} }. Use cases: access variables/bindings outside handlers, global context access across functions. Context methods: c.set(), c.var, c.env. Error handling: getContext throws if context unavailable, tryGetContext safe returns undefined. Questions: How to access context globally? sections.manifest: Import statements for Context Storage middleware. import {Hono} from 'hono' for the main framework class. import {contextStorage, getContext, tryGetContext} from 'hono/context-storage' for middleware and accessor functions. Questions: What to import? Where are these located?

Context Storage usage patterns. Pattern 1: Variables outside handlers. Type Env with Variables: {message: string}. app.use(contextStorage()). c.set('message', 'Hello!'). Access with getContext<Env>().var.message outside handler functions. Allows retrieval across function boundaries. Pattern 2: Cloudflare Workers bindings. Type Env with Bindings: {KV: KVNamespace}. getContext<Env>().env.KV.put('key', value). Call KV methods outside handler. Works because context stored in AsyncLocalStorage. tryGetContext() function: safe context access variant. Works like getContext() but returns undefined if context unavailable. Type: tryGetContext<Env>(). Returns undefined if outside contextStorage() scope. Safe null-check pattern: if (context) { ... use context ... }. No error thrown. Useful for defensive programming. Difference from getContext(): getContext() throws, tryGetContext() returns undefined. Questions: When to use tryGetContext? What's the difference from getContext? How to handle missing context? When is context unavailable?
